text: In a surface-EMG comparison, the behind-the-neck lat pulldown gave no advantage for the lats over the front pulldown, and the authors advise preferring the front version.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Sperandei conclusion. Healthy trained men only. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: Pulldown grips from one to two times shoulder width gave similar lat, trapezius and infraspinatus activity; the widest grip allowed slightly less load.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Andersen. Fifteen men. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: In pull-ups and chin-ups, the lats worked hardest, then biceps, with lower trapezius more active in the pull-up and chest and biceps more in the chin-up.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Youdas 2010. Healthy adults. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: The inverted row loaded the lumbar spine less than a standing bent-over row while still working the lats and upper back.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Fenwick; seven men. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: The standing bent-over row gave the largest lumbar spine load of the rows tested.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Fenwick. Does not test a bench-supported dumbbell row. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: During an inverted row, healthy people recruited the muscles that move and steady the shoulder blade.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Youdas 2020. Does not show it treats shoulder pain. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: Push-ups with the hands raised on a box produced lower ground force than a regular push-up, so they are a lighter version.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Ebben. Measures ground force, not muscle activity. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: Push-ups with hands closer than shoulder width produced more chest and triceps activity than wide hands.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Cogley. One repetition per position. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: A standard dumbbell curl and an incline dumbbell curl showed similar biceps long-head activity across the movement; the preacher version differed.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Oliveira 2009. Biceps long head only. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.

text: Seated or standing, and dumbbell or barbell, changed how hard the deltoids and arm muscles worked in the shoulder press.

review.notes: Paraphrase of Saeterbakken 2013. Healthy men. Graded C: single lab study, not a guideline or systematic review; confirm.
